text: On the last night I pressed three gold coins into my doubles hand and, on a sudden impulse, put my own white hat on his head to shield it from the tropical sun. <break time="0.8s" /> Our hands met gropingly, lingered for a second, and parted, and he slipped out through a port in the sail locker as silently as he had first come out of the sea. <break time="0.8s" /> Under the pretext of seeking the land breezes, I then steered toward Koh ring, a great black island, far closer than any prudent seaman would have dared to go. <break time="0.8s" /> The island loomed so high above our masts that it seemed to hang over the ship, and my chief mate, losing all control of himself, cried out that we would be wrecked. <break time="0.8s" /> In that dreadful darkness I could not tell whether the ship was moving at all, until I saw, floating close by, the white hat I had given him, left behind upon the water. <break time="0.8s" /> It served me as a mark, showing that she was gathering sternway, and I gave the order to shift the helm, so that she came round slowly and stood away from the land. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, alone at last with my command, I thought of the secret sharer of my cabin, who had lowered himself into the water to take his punishment, a free man, a proud swimmer striking out for a new destiny.
